summary.text: Rebecca Saldaña represents Washington's 37th Legislative District, which includes parts of South Seattle and Renton, in the state Senate. Her official biography says she was appointed to the Senate in 2016 and chairs the Senate Labor & Commerce Committee.

paragraphs.text: Saldaña grew up in Seattle's Delridge neighborhood, according to her official biography, and earned a degree in theology and humanities from Seattle University.
It says her father was a Mexican immigrant and former farmworker who became a machinist and her mother was a social worker.

After college, the page says she worked in labor and community organizing with Oregon's farmworker union PCUN, the United Farm Workers and SEIU Local 6, and later served as executive director of Puget Sound Sage.
The page says she was appointed to the state Senate in 2016 and that she also serves on the Agriculture & Natural Resources, Rules and Ways & Means committees.
It credits her with sponsoring and passing the HEAL Act and the Washington Voting Rights Act, and says she lives in the Rainier Beach/Skyway area with her husband and their two youngest children.
